item.title: Some actors don’t love fame; they just love acting – Lolade Okusanya
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress and The Unserious Podcast co-host Lolade Okusanya has said some actors are more interested in their craft than the fame that comes with it. Okusanya made this observation while discussing celebrity privacy on the podcast, citing veteran actresses Genevieve Nnaji and Omotola Jalade Ekeinde as examples of public figures who have sought a more private life despite their fame. “There are people like Genevieve; after all the fame, they went back into their shells. They still have the fame, but they want to go back into their shells. Omotola Jalade Ekeinde too, she went back into her shell,” she said. According to the actress, celebrities may desire privacy, but public attention can make it difficult for them to maintain personal boundaries. She noted that fans may still approach celebrities for photographs when they encounter them in public, regardless of their preference for a quieter life. “Because no matter how much she still craves that private life, we will disrupt it,” Okusanya said. She added that not every actor is motivated by the prospect of fame, explaining that some are primarily passionate about acting itself. “Some actors do not love fame; they just love acting. But some jobs come with fame,” she said. Her comments highlight the tension between public recognition and personal privacy in the entertainment industry, where professional visibility can make it difficult for celebrities to maintain a life away from public attention. item.title: Burna Boy’s incredible first feats that set Afrobeats ablaze in the world
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Destiny does not always play fair. Sometimes, it goes overboard or hits below the belt. It is convenient to see Burna Boy today as the “African Giant” without paying much attention to the circumstances that brought the moniker about. It was, in fact, a controversy that Damini Ogulu, popularly known as Burna Boy, took advantage of after feeling diminished and disrespected. Burna Boy’s “African Giant” moniker originated from a 2019 controversy over the size of his name on the Coachella music festival’s promotional poster. What began as a protest against how he was billed eventually became the title of his breakthrough album and a defining identity in his career. Yet, in retrospect, destiny was playing fair, with an all-seeing eye. In response to the perceived disrespect, he took to social media to assert his stature, describing himself as an “African Giant”. The statement attracted considerable attention, with some Nigerians criticising him as arrogant, while others supported his insistence that African musicians deserved greater recognition. If respect is earned rather than demanded, Burna Boy is an exception. He demanded it and earned it. His achievements on the global stage as an African artiste tell the whole story, and 2026 has been a stupendous year for the *Twice as Tall* global hitmaker. In less than one week, he has recorded two historic firsts: performing at the NFL’s first regular-season game in France and becoming the first Nigerian artiste to present an award at the Ballon d’Or. These milestones follow his World Cup feat, where he performed alongside Colombian superstar Shakira at the first-ever halftime show at a FIFA World Cup final, helping bring Afrobeats to one of football’s biggest global stages. Burna Boy also made history as the first Afrobeats artiste to perform on the Grammy Awards stage. His performance featured Brandy and 21 Savage, marking a significant moment for the genre at the prestigious US music ceremony. In July 2023, Burna Boy became the first African artiste to sell out a stadium in the United States when he performed at Citi Field in New York. The milestone demonstrated the commercial appeal of African music in the American live-music market. In the same vein, Burna Boy headlined the 80,000-capacity London Stadium during his *Love, Damini* tour, becoming the first African artiste to headline the venue. The concert was another landmark for African performers in the United Kingdom. Burna Boy also performed at the opening ceremony of the UEFA Champions League final in Istanbul, Turkey, sharing the stage with Brazilian singer Anitta. The appearance placed Nigerian music before a huge international football audience. He further joined Tems and Rema for a performance at the NBA All-Star Game halftime show in Salt Lake City, Utah. item.title: There’s more to women than sexuality – Bukola Ikuomola
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Actress and filmmaker Bukola Ikuomola, popularly known as MZNicollet, has said women should be recognised for their intellect, achievements and contributions to society rather than their sexuality. In a chat with Potpourri, Ikuomola, who expressed her views on women flaunting their sexuality on social media, said she admired women who distinguished themselves through their intelligence and accomplishments. “There is more to women than sexuality. I admire women who are known for their intellect and other great achievements,” she said. The Ondo State-born actress, who also has Urhobo roots in Warri, Delta State, said she developed a passion for acting from an early age and had always admired the profession. She is a graduate of Novena University, Ogume, Delta State, and also runs Nickiscollections as its chief executive officer. Speaking about the sacrifices she has made to build her acting career, Ikuomola said she had invested considerable time, effort and the little money available to her in improving her craft. She described working with veteran actors, including Saheed Balogun, Jobola Dabo, Ayo Mogaji and Muyiwa Ademola, as some of her memorable experiences in the industry. She also expressed pride in producing her first movie, *Enemy Within*. On the kind of roles she enjoys playing, Ikuomola said she preferred heroic characters who demonstrate strength and determination and contribute meaningfully to a story. However, she noted that her versatility allows her to approach different roles with passion. The actress said her ambition was to become a megastar with an international reputation, extending her influence beyond Nollywood. On relationships, Ikuomola said respect and a good sense of humour were qualities she valued in a man, adding that she preferred men to make the first move. She also declared a preference for money over love, explaining that past experiences had left her feeling used in relationships because of how much she gave to the people she loved. “Now I go for money. And if love comes with it, I grab it too,” she said, adding that love becomes sweeter when money is involved. item.title: How Real Warri Pikin conquered comedy stages across continents
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi When Nigerian comedian and actor Anita Alaire Asuoha, popularly known as Real Warri Pikin, won the Best Stand-Up Comedian award at the 2026 African Muzik Magazine Awards (AFRIMMA), it marked another milestone in a career built on hard work, persistence and an unmistakable brand of humour. The honour, presented at the awards ceremony held in Dallas, Texas, on September 12, placed her ahead of several established comedy stars, including Basketmouth, Bovi, Godfrey, Eric Omondi, Trevor Noah, Patrick “Salvado” Idringi and Ty Ngachira. Her victory was a significant recognition of her growing influence in African comedy and her expanding international profile. <u> </u> “This award means a lot to me because it is a recognition of the journey, the work and the years of showing up even when I didn’t know where it would lead,” she said. “To be recognised as Best Comedian at AFRIMMA, representing Nigeria and Africa, is a huge honour. It also reminds me that staying true to who you are and using your story to connect with people can take you places you never imagined,” she added. For Asuoha, the AFRIMMA triumph represents more than a trophy. It reflects years of building an entertainment career that spans stand-up comedy, acting, digital content creation, live shows and television and web productions. Known for her energetic stage presence, Warri-inflected expressions and use of Nigerian Pidgin, Real Warri Pikin has developed a comic identity rooted in everyday experiences, relationships and the peculiarities of Nigerian life. Her ability to turn familiar situations into humorous stories has helped her connect with audiences across different age groups and cultural backgrounds. Her journey from online comedy skits to major entertainment stages has also demonstrated the growing opportunities available to Nigerian comedians who can build audiences through digital platforms and translate that popularity into live performances. One of the defining projects in her career is “Real Warri Pikin Unfiltered”, a comedy show that expanded beyond Nigeria to audiences in Ghana and the United Kingdom, including Milton Keynes, Manchester and London. The show established her ability to headline performances outside her home country while retaining the distinctive humour that first endeared her to Nigerian audiences. She has also performed at established Nigerian comedy platforms and events, including “AY Live”, “Warri Again?” and Bovi’s “Man on Fire”, sharing stages with some of the country’s recognised entertainers. Her international ambitions gathered further momentum in 2026 with the “In My Element” tour. The American leg included performances in Dallas and Houston, Texas, while the Canadian leg covered Winnipeg, Toronto, London, Saskatoon, Regina and Vancouver. The Canadian run was reported as a sold-out six-city tour, underlining her appeal among Nigerians and other African comedy enthusiasts living abroad. item.title: Mixed reactions trail Zlatan’s wedding
item.description: By Sarah Ammah Nigerian street-pop star Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael, popularly known as Zlatan Ibile, has sparked conversations online following his traditional wedding to his longtime partner, Davita Lamai, in Lagos on October 24, 2026. The glamorous ceremony attracted celebrities, including singer Davido, who served as one of the groomsmen. The couple impressed guests with their traditional outfits and colourful cultural displays, making the celebration a major talking point on social media. While many fans congratulated the couple and praised their outfits, others focused on Davita’s appearance, with some social media users making negative comments about her looks. Another issue that generated debate was Zlatan’s decision to marry Davita after they had already welcomed two children together. Some critics questioned why he chose to marry a woman who already had two children for him, while others defended the couple, arguing that their relationship and decision to marry were nobody else’s business. The wedding also attracted attention following Nollywood actress Joke Jigan’s comments about the absence of popular “Lagos baddies” at the event, which generated mixed reactions online. Despite the criticism, many fans celebrated the couple’s union and praised Zlatan for taking the next step in his relationship with Davita. Ultimately, the wedding became more than a celebration of love, turning into a social media debate about beauty standards, relationships, marriage and public opinion. item.title: Chacx, African China collaborate on ‘Forgive’
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nigerian singer Chacx has collaborated with veteran musician African China on his new single, Forgive, released on Friday, October 30. The collaboration brings the emerging singer together with African China, known for his street-inspired music and socially conscious themes. Speaking about the collaboration, Chacx expressed excitement about working with the veteran singer, describing the experience as an opportunity to learn from an established voice in Nigerian music. “Working with African China is an exciting experience for me. I have great respect for his journey and the connection his music has built with audiences over the years. Collaborating with him gave me an opportunity to exchange creative ideas and approach the song from different perspectives. I believe working with artistes from different generations can broaden your understanding of music and challenge you to grow. I am glad to have him on Forgive and look forward to listeners experiencing what we have created together,” Chacx said. Chacx, whose real name is Manu Charles Chukwuye, began his professional music career in 2019 with Obi Mo, featuring Cme2k. His subsequent releases include the EPs New Beginning (2021) and Advanced (2023), alongside songs such as Blessed, featuring Portable and Shocker Lo Se Beat, Hold Me, Baby Girl, Feelings and Fake Friends. In 2026, he signed with Homeboy International Music Label, adding another development to his career. With Forgive, Chacx brings his sound together with African China’s established musical identity in a collaboration that introduces a new release to both artistes’ catalogues. item.title: Congolese singer Agressivo Nyandoro targets Nigerian market
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Congolese singer and songwriter Agressivo Nyandoro has identified Nigeria as one of the African markets he hopes to reach as he seeks to expand his music beyond the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The musician, who began his musical journey as a guitarist in 2009 before releasing his own music in 2012, said he wants his songs to connect with audiences across the continent while retaining the cultural identity that shaped his sound. “Looking ahead, I would like my music to reach more people outside the DRC. Nigeria interests me, as do other African markets where music circulates widely,” Nyandoro said. Known for drawing inspiration from everyday experiences, the Lubumbashi-born musician incorporates storytelling into his songs, exploring human relationships, family responsibilities and social issues. He said his approach to music goes beyond entertainment. “I would simply say that I am a message. When I sing, I am not just trying to make people dance. I also want to tell them something, help them understand a situation, or encourage them to think about what is happening around them,” he said. His song, Jonathan, explores infidelity, an absent husband and the consequences of neglecting family responsibilities. According to the singer, the story reflects situations he has observed in society. Nyandoro is also pursuing cross-border collaborations, having worked with Tanzanian musician Stamina Shorwebwenzi and Shakis Boy on Ipo Siku (Remix). His EP, Déterminé, features Congolese artistes Celeo Scram and Jaysix Abdallah. He believes such collaborations can help African musicians reach audiences beyond their home countries. “An artist from the DRC can reach an audience in Tanzania, just as a Tanzanian artist can introduce their music to Congolese listeners,” he said. Nyandoro is scheduled to perform at Espace Village Chez Ntemba in Kinshasa on October 31, 2026, as he continues working towards expanding his audience. item.title: Shuga Band immortalises late founder, Akiin Shuga with new innovations
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nigeria’s foremost premium live music ensemble, Shuga Band is marking the first anniversary of its late founder, Akinloye Tofowomo popularly known as Akiin Shuga by reinventing its brand identity with the launch of a new logo asset to immortalize his glorious memory. The band dedicated the entire month of October to celebrate its late founder with the unveiling of the new brand identity across all owned media platforms. It also reinforced her new look identity at all her engagements in the month of October. Signifying professionalism and excellence in music, the new identity carries the face of the widely-regarded founder holding a mic and doing what he knew how to do best for the larger part of his life. Further deepening the legacy, the band released Best of Akiin Shuga on digital platforms, a compilation of his life performances. These deep values have kept the band going for over two and a half decade making it a reference point in the pantheon of live music. The latest effort is another layer to deepen a strong structure around the band in its post-founder phase. While unveiling a Valentine medley for lovers earlier in the year, the band also announced the constitution of a high-calibre advisory board to provide oversight and direction.. Shuga band has been proving doubters wrong and converting them to clients and lovers one show at a time. It continues to enjoy patronage from event planners, vendors and fans alike. Among its recent back-to-back performances include the high-octane 60th birthday shindig of Dr Muiz Banire’s 60th birthday day party, Seplat Nigerian Content Day, Prince Nduka Obaigbena’s 67th birthday, FCMB Sheventures and Shuttlers’s 10th anniversary among a host of others. Still maintaining her founder, Akiin Shuga’s signature music repertoire and flawlessly delivered, the band continues to wow guests. Shuga Band is known for her eclectic sound switching seamlessly among genres such as classics, traditional, gospel and contemporary. “Our founder, Akiin Shuga, taught us that music is service to people, to God and joy itself. He advocated for a structured industry built on integrity, trust and professionalism, and our ability to sustain his legacy is a testament to those values,” says Maria Tofowomo, COO, Shuga Band. Also speaking, Jerry Odeh, Business Manager, “We are grateful for the support that we have enjoyed from all our stakeholders in the last one year. The strong values of service, excellence and professionalism established by our founder and maestro, Akiin Shuga has been our compass. With such a solid legacy backbone, Shuga Band is now being established as a generational brand. We will continue to innovate and ensure effective service delivery for all our stakeholders.” Explaining more, he also revealed that activities of the Shuga Limb Foundation, a passion project of the late founder and anti-polio champion has not stopped making impact. item.title: Enkay Ogboruche wins Africa Gospel Music Impact Award at Clima Awards 2026
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Award-winning worship leader and recording artiste Nkiruka Gift Ogboruche, popularly known as Enkay Ogboruche, has been named winner of the Africa Gospel Music Impact Award at the 2026 Clima Awards Africa, held on the 9th of October 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria. The award honours gospel ministers whose sound has crossed borders and shaped worship culture across the continent. It comes at the peak of a landmark year for the singer. Over more than a decade, Enkay has grown from humble beginnings into one of Africa’s most respected worship voices. She has released three albums, *The Kingdom Anthem* (2015), *The Bridge* (2018) and *Declaration* (2023), and has given the global church anthems such as “Yes, You Are The Lord” and “Salute,” the latter featuring Grammy winner Kierra Sheard. Her influence extends well beyond the microphone. She is the convener of Enkay Live in Concert, Pneuma Worship Experience and Alabanza, and the founder of The Spotlight, a platform dedicated to discovering and mentoring the next generation of gospel talent. The latest recognition follows her win as Diaspora Female Artiste of the Year at the 2026 Nigeria International Gospel Music Awards (NIGMA) and her induction into the 2026 new class of the Recording Academy (Grammy), placing her among a growing number of African music professionals shaping global music conversations at the highest level. Enkay has often described her ministry as a blend of discipline, growth and grace, a journey that has taken her from local church platforms to international stages, including Liberty University’s Global Night of Worship alongside Michael W. Smith. Industry watchers say the award is well deserved, citing not only her vocal excellence and consistent hits but also her decade-long commitment to promoting authentic worship and exporting African gospel music to the world. With her fourth album in the works, Enkay Ogboruche continues to show that African gospel music has both the message and the mastery to impact the world. item.title: Ufuoma Okonoko unveils digital strategy to unlock billions for Nigeria’s creative sector
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Barrister Ufuoma Okonoko, a digital monetisation expert and Chief Operating Officer of Atlantic World Digital Communications, has unveiled a digital strategy aimed at unlocking billions of dollars in international revenue for Nigeria’s creative sector through strategic distribution, marketing and commercialisation of locally produced content and products. Okonoko, who is also a Nollywood actress and producer known professionally as Angel Ufuoma, said Nigeria’s creative industry holds enormous potential to generate foreign exchange, identifying filmmaking, Afrobeats, fashion, culinary arts, publishing, pharmaceuticals, arts and crafts, and tourism as sectors that could benefit from improved access to international markets. She explained that the strategy informed the development of Blaze Channel, a United States-based digital monetisation platform designed to distribute and generate revenue from Nigerian films while creating international markets for other products and services within the country’s creative economy. According to her, the initiative is intended to address the persistent difficulties filmmakers encounter in generating adequate revenue from their productions, while leveraging the international appeal of Nollywood and Afrobeats to introduce other Nigerian products to global consumers. “Nollywood filmmakers produce great films, but they find it very difficult to monetise them. We created Blaze Channel as a digital monetisation platform in the USA, not only to stream and monetise the movies, but more importantly to monetise Nigerian Creative Industry products,” she said. Okonoko explained that the strategy would use films and music to attract international audiences before introducing them to other Nigerian products, including fashion items, culinary offerings, publishing materials, pharmaceutical products, artificial intelligence solutions, and arts and crafts available for purchase by consumers overseas. She said the approach was designed to go beyond conventional film distribution by creating a broader commercial ecosystem in which Nigerian entertainment content could serve as a gateway for other homegrown businesses seeking access to international markets. According to her, the model could also stimulate interest in Nigeria as a tourism destination and encourage foreign direct investment by exposing international audiences to the country’s cultural assets, creative talent and business opportunities. The company disclosed that Okonoko spent 10 years working with software engineers in the United States to develop the platform before its official launch in 2018. Since then, Blaze Channel has attracted more than 2,000 subscribers worldwide. item.title: Lilian Nneji set to release 16-track album, “Highly Favoured” November 6
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Award-winning Nigerian gospel music minister, songwriter, and worship leader Lilian Nneji is set to release her highly anticipated album, Highly Favored, on November 6, 2026. The forthcoming 16-track project promises to be a remarkable musical experience, bringing together different genres and expressions of gospel music while celebrating God’s faithfulness, goodness, mercy, and unfailing love. Known for her energetic praise expressions, powerful vocals, and distinctive ability to lead audiences into heartfelt worship, Lilian Nneji is preparing to deliver an album that caters to listeners across different generations. One of the exciting features of Highly Favored is its musical diversity. The project brings together beautiful praise sounds that resonate with the older generation and vibrant, energetic contemporary gospel expressions that connect with younger listeners. From traditional gospel influences to high-energy praise and deeply reflective worship, the album offers something for everyone. The 16-track project will feature some of Lilian Nneji’s familiar and much-loved songs, including “Omeriwo Omeriwo Reprise” and “If E Reach Your Turn,” alongside other inspiring musical offerings. The complete tracklist includes: 1. Do For You 2. Wonderful 3. Mercy 4. Omeriwo Omeriwo Reprise 5. If E Reach Your Turn 6. I’m Active 7. Eze Mu O 8. Grateful 9. Elohim 10. E Get Why 11. Daalu 12. Ntughari 13. Odogwu N’agha 14. LNG Praise Medley 15. Mi O Le Gbagbe 16. Onwere Ihe Omere Mụ With a ministry built around energetic praise, thanksgiving, and unwavering faith in God, Lilian Nneji has consistently blessed audiences through songs such as If E Reach Your Turn, E Get Why, Mercy, Odogwu N’agha, and Onwere Ihe Omere Mụ. Fondly known as “Energy,” “Odogwu,” and “Praise Machine,” she has become a familiar voice in the Nigerian gospel music scene, captivating audiences with her energetic stage presence and powerful renditions of indigenous gospel music. Her ministry journey has also attracted significant recognition, including Africa Praise Artiste of the Year 2024 at the Clima Africa Awards, Praise Minstrel of the Year 2024 at the Global Merit Awards, and Africa Most Outstanding Gospel Music Minister (Stage Category) 2025 at the Clima Africa Awards. Most recently, in October 2026, she was named Africa Gospel Artiste of the Year at the Clima Africa Awards, further affirming her growing influence in the gospel music industry. As anticipation builds towards the release, Highly Favored promises to be more than just another album. It is a musical celebration of God’s goodness, a reminder of His faithfulness, and an invitation for listeners of every generation to express their gratitude through praise and worship. item.title: Orijin lights up Felabration, celebrating Fela’s legacy
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Culture evolves when heritage meets new forms of expression. Across Nigeria, indigenous traditions continue to find relevance through music, dance, fashion, and digital storytelling, shaping how younger generations experience and express their identity. For Orijin, the number 1 premium bitters brand, this intersection presents an opportunity to do more than celebrate culture; it is an opportunity to participate meaningfully in its evolution. This thinking informed Orijin’s presence at Felabration 2026, held in Lagos from October 16 to 18. The annual festival celebrating the life and legacy of Afrobeat pioneer Fela Anikulapo-Kuti provided a fitting platform for the brand to connect indigenous heritage with the contemporary creative energy shaping Nigeria’s cultural landscape. For Orijin, the partnership went beyond visibility at a major music festival. It reflected a deliberate approach to engaging with cultural platforms where tradition, creativity and contemporary lifestyles intersect. By participating in an event associated with artistic freedom, cultural identity and creative expression, Orijin sought to create experiences that bring indigenous heritage into conversations that resonate with today’s audiences. At the heart of this approach is the belief that tradition and modernity are complementary. Cultural heritage remains relevant when people can experience it in new settings, share it across generations and reinterpret it through contemporary forms of expression. Through partnerships such as Felabration, Orijin is creating opportunities for these connections to take shape. The festival provided a natural setting for this ambition. Rooted in Fela’s enduring influence on music and social expression, Felabration brings together Nigeria’s musical heritage and evolving creative culture. Within this environment, Orijin introduced indigenous performances that demonstrated how traditional art forms can find fresh relevance in contemporary spaces. On Saturday, Oriki and dance performances brought indigenous storytelling and movement into the festival experience. Oriki, particularly within Yoruba culture, is a form of praise poetry that preserves ancestry, identity, family history, and communal memory. Presented alongside contemporary music, it illustrated how expressions deeply rooted in tradition can engage audiences in modern cultural settings. Beyond the performances, Orijin encouraged direct participation through conversations with festivalgoers about their experiences, including whether they were attending Felabration for the first time and how they preferred to enjoy Orijin. Merchandise was presented to participants in appreciation of their involvement, while influencers documented performances and audience interactions, extending the experience to their online communities. item.title: Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests
item.description: …Two suspected cases test negative after two rounds of laboratory tests By Chioma Obinna The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) last night said two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests, assuring Nigerians that the confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection reported in the country. The agency said the two individuals, who presented with symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated as public health authorities commenced investigations and appropriate response measures. In a press statement yesterday, the Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the report was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) in the early hours of October 30, 2026. He said samples collected from the individuals were subjected to laboratory testing to establish the cause of their illness, adding that both tested negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing. “Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said. He clarified that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Adamawa, stressing that the index case previously confirmed in the FCT remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria. “At this juncture, I wish to commend the efforts of the Adamawa State’s Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive approach. NCDC will continue to provide appropriate technical support to the Adamawa State Government to strengthen their response operations,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja involving a traveller who arrived in Nigeria from Uganda. The emergence of the suspected cases in Adamawa had raised concerns about a possible spread of the disease, prompting the state and federal health authorities to activate investigation and precautionary measures. However, the negative laboratory results have ruled out Ebola infection in the two individuals, based on the tests reported by the NCDC. Idris urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about the situation. “We urge members of the public to remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information or speculation about the situation. The public is encouraged to obtain information from official government and public health communication channels,” he said. The NCDC director-general, however, emphasised the need for continued vigilance, noting that Ebola was a serious infectious disease requiring prompt identification, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures. item.title: Barca hammer Alaves 6-1 to retain Liga top spot
item.description: Raphinha and Lamine Yamal struck twice each as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats. Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou. Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend’s La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick’s side found their groove once more. Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca’s sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. There was a minute’s silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga’s top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form. Midfield maestro Pedri played in Lopez, who pulled the ball across for the Brazil international to bundle home. Alaves came close through Abde Rebbach before Lopez doubled Barcelona’s lead in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, Lopez smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca’s lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca’s fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca’s sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. – Seven in a row – Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone’s Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. item.title: Ortom hits back at ex-envoy Tarzoor, highlights governance achievements
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Former Benue State Governor, Chief Samuel Ortom, has challenged Ambassador Terhemen Tarzoor to account for his record in public office, accusing him of sustained attacks on his person over the defeat he suffered during the 2015 governorship election in the state. Recall that the former Nigerian envoy to Namibia had, during a recent media outing criticised the former governor over what he described as uncomplimentary remarks about Governor Hyacinth Alia and his administration. Ortom described Tarzoor’s criticism as “a manifestation of the bitterness he has harboured since his defeat in the 2015 governorship election,” alleging that the former governorship candidate had consistently used media engagements to attack him more than a decade after the election. He said Tarzoor’s latest comments, ostensibly in defence of Governor Hyacinth Alia, were an attempt to remain politically relevant. He added that the ambassador had misrepresented his remarks by claiming that he described the actions of the people of Benue as “shenanigans.” “Chief Ortom could never have used such a term to disparage the people of Benue State. If anything, his reference was to the antics of individuals like Tarzoor, whose utterances and conduct appear calculated to sow discord, deepen divisions and breed acrimony in the polity,” he said. Ina statement.by his media Aide, Paul Zege, the former governor questioned Tarzoor’s record as Speaker of the Benue State House of Assembly, asking him to identify the developmental projects he attracted to his constituency and the achievements he could point to as evidence of his contributions to the people. He also raised questions about the controversial creation of a Fulani ward in Makurdi Local Government Area, LGA, which he said was subsequently reversed after the exercise was reportedly found to be fraudulent. Ortom further questioned Tarzoor’s record as Nigeria’s ambassador to Namibia, alleging that his tenure failed to establish a notable diplomatic legacy, urging the former Speaker to focus on issues affecting the state rather than engage in what he described as persistent attacks on him. Defending his administration’s record, Ortom said security was one of the defining issues of his tenure, particularly his opposition to open grazing and the repeated attacks on farming communities. He said his administration “enacted the Open Grazing Prohibition and Ranches Establishment Law of 2017, established the Benue State Livestock Guards, supported the Community Volunteer Guards and provided logistics to security agencies. “He could have chosen the politically convenient path. He could have remained silent, avoided confrontation with powerful interests and maintained cordial relations with the Federal Government of the day. Instead, he chose to stand with his people and defend their lands when he believed the survival of his people was at stake,” he said. item.title: 2027: Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu, South-East govs tell Igbos
item.description: Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, and health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said. The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the federal government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development. “We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said. item.description: Fabio Silva’s 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy levelled shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal. In the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils. “Coming back twice here in Munich is no easy feat. We earned a well-deserved point here today,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side “never stopped believing in ourselves.” Dortmund’s Guinean forward #09 Serhou Guirassy (C) scores the 1-1 goal during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 ‘Klassiker’ matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious. item.title: Clashes Erupt In France As Thousands Protest Cost Of Living, Inequality
item.description: A police officer in Paris was injured after being struck by a Molotov cocktail as clashes erupted in the capital and other cities during protests across France against soaring living costs and inequality. Hundreds of thousands of people, some dressed for Halloween, demonstrated across France in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations. But the Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pointed to an “extraordinary” level of violence from some, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces. He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an “attempted murder,” adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. ‘Engulfed In Flames’ Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the Molotov attack must be “punished with the utmost severity.” “The images of a police officer engulfed in flames after being targeted with incendiary devices are unbearable,” Le Pen said on X. A French riot gendarme mobile has flames rising up his uniform after being hit by a Molotov cocktail during a charge against demonstrators at the end of a demonstration part of a nationwide day of protests over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organisations, in Paris on October 31, 2026. Photo by SAMEER AL-DOUMY / AFP A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods from 11:00 pm to 6:00 am on Saturday and Sunday. Police arrested more than 420 people across the country. The interior ministry said that “radical elements” in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres “with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting”. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people. ‘Attack On Freedom’ Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. item.title: German Police, Protesters Clash After ‘Gen Z’ Protest, Several Police Officers Injured
item.description: German police and protesters clashed across the country Saturday following massive youth-led protests, with authorities using water cannon and pepper spray as masked demonstrators hurled fireworks, stones and bottles. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined protests nationwide that were organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police were pelted with projectiles in the western city of Frankfurt, and responded by using water cannon and pepper spray as they sought to clear protesters. “Incidents of stones and fireworks being thrown at the emergency services continue to occur,” police said on X. “We are taking action against these troublemakers.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. ‘Boiling Point’ In Berlin, a protest that was not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. Police detain a protester after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere, with some dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.They waved signs that read “Time for resistance”, and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “I think it’s really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France,” Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin. “I’ve been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step.” Marius, a 23-year-old care worker, added that “politicians need to know about this… the situation is slowly reaching boiling point.” “I think we can all feel that this just isn’t working anymore,” he added. The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. item.title: Binance says has covered 90% of $6.3 billion hack losses
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Saturday it has used company money to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of $6.3 billion stolen in a huge hacking attack. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X. Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, said the remaining 10 percent of tokens are “less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts.” The company said it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack. Binance said Friday it was working to resolve what it called a “complex attack” with several “points of breach.” Investigators pointed to hackers linked to North Korea as being responsible. The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack. Binance suspended user withdrawals after the incident, but said in its latest update they were on track to resume Sunday. The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. President Donald Trump said Friday the United States was looking into the hack, and the FBI said it was “engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity” and was ready to investigate. item.title: Insecurity didn’t begin in Tinubu’s administration – Dogara
item.description: A former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Mr Yakubu Dogara, says Nigeria’s security challenges predate the administration of President Bola Tinubu. Dogara, who is the Chancellor of Achievers University, Owo, Ondo State, made the assertion at the institution’s 16th convocation ceremony, where 836 graduands received various academic qualifications. He said terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence had been entrenched in the country long before the current administration assumed office in May 2023. According to him, the nation’s security problems are rooted in years of porous borders, illegal arms proliferation, high youth unemployment and the spread of extremist ideologies. “Insecurity in Nigeria did not begin with this administration. This is no excuse, because the facts need no defence. Terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence did not arrive in 2023,” Dogara said. He explained that the security situation developed over several years, stressing that its roots went deep long before the current government took over. Dogara, however, noted that President Tinubu had consistently identified national security as a top priority and major responsibility of his administration. The chancellor charged the graduands to deploy their talents, creativity and innovation toward national development. Speaking, the Pro-Chancellor of the university, Prof. Bode Ayorinde, acknowledged the progress made in expanding access to tertiary education, but expressed concern over the job prospects of graduates. Ayorinde cited figures from the National Universities Commission (NUC), which put the number of universities in Nigeria at 312 as of June 2026, comprising 77 federal, 67 state-owned, and 168 private institutions. He said although the growth represented a huge investment in human capital by parents, governments and lecturers, deliberate efforts must be made to create viable opportunities for graduates after school. In her address, the Vice-Chancellor of the institution, Prof. Omolola Irinoye, reiterated the university’s commitment to providing quality education that combines intellectual growth, practical skills, character building and social responsibility. Irinoye said that there were 98 First Class graduates in the academic session, attributing the performance to the institution’s investment in quality assurance, staff development and a conducive learning environment. According to her, the university also operates flexible payment arrangements to accommodate students from different socioeconomic backgrounds. “The institution’s scholarship programme was designed to ensure that financial constraints did not prevent deserving students from acquiring university education. “The university has 100 per cent tuition scholarship in 17 academic programmes, with 80 per cent tuition scholarship in five academic programmes while there were also 70 per cent tuition scholarship in other five academic programmes,” she said. item.title: Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident
item.description: The Katsina State Government has dismissed reports linking the incident that occurred in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to Governor Dikko Radda’s Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign, describing such claims as false and misleading. In a statement, the government said preliminary findings showed that the disturbance stemmed from a disagreement between participants in a Maulud procession and security personnel over designated procession routes, resulting in confusion along a public street in Yankara. It stressed that the incident was entirely unrelated to thegovernor’s campaign activities or the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally held in Faskari. According to the government, Governor Radda passed through Yankara without incident on his way to Faskari, where he paid a courtesy visit to the District Head’s Palace and was received by the district head and other traditional rulers. The governor, it said, later proceeded to the Faskari Local Government secretariat, where he inspected ongoing renovation works at the secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally and interacting with residents and supporters. Governor Dikko Radda addresses a crowd of supporters at the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign in Faskari Local Government Area of Katsina State on October 31, 2026. The state government urged relevant security agencies to carry out a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that those responsible are identified where necessary. In the statement signed by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ibrahim Mohammed, the government appealed to residents to remain calm, uphold peace, and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary tension. Violence was reported in Yankara town on Saturday after suspected hoodlums attacked supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), leaving several people injured and a campaign vehicle set ablaze. Eyewitnesses said the attackers allegedly ambushed APC supporters heading to Governor Radda’s campaign rally in Faskari, disrupting movement along the major road and causing panic among residents. Angry youths were also alleged to have blocked the route the campaign convoy was expected to use. item.title: Man City Stunned In 0-1 Home Loss To Brighton
item.description: Manchester City suffered a second straight Premier League defeat at the hands of Brighton with a 1-0 win as the Seagulls went close within two points of the leaders on Saturday. Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first-ever away win against City on their 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title. The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials. Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead. Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time. Manchester City’s Norwegian striker Erling Haaland reacts following the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld, they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. Defeat for Maresca’s men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. item.title: Africa’s First Ever Youth Olympics Open In Senegal
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, opened Saturday in the Senegalese capital, marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are omnipresent across Dakar, which is hosting nearly 2,700 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event will see the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the young athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “Today it’s not just a nation that is welcoming the Youth Olympic Games; it’s an entire continent that is opening its arms”, Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye told a sport and development summit Saturday ahead of the Games’ opening ceremony. Senegal’s Influencer and TikToker Khaby Lame carries the Youth Olympic Flame on the eve of the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on October 30, 2026. Photo by PATRICK MEINHARDT / AFP The Games will not only celebrate champions but also “our collective capacity to transform sport into an economic and social engine”, he said, emphasising that 130 years of Olympic history had passed before the Olympic flame ever landed on African soil. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly, located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events. The Games are “showing the world our capacity (as Africa), a capacity that sometimes is underestimated”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Saturday during the summit. According to Coventry, the opening ceremony will be televised live in more than 30 countries, with every African nation having committed to showing the Games live, she said. Sports Culture An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games. A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event. The West African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene. Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or on weekends on the beach or in village squares. And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise. While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics has struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal. Mexican athletes arrive with their suitcases at the Youth Olympic Village in Diamniadio, on October 29, 2026.
